questions.q: What is the net invoice amount for SO-48217 after the volume discount, and what invoice number does it become?
questions.explain: After the 5% volume discount, SO-48217's 400 control panels net to $55,100.00, invoiced as INV-HV-30144.

questions.q: What new natural account does shipping SO-48217 bring into play, beyond Product Revenue?
questions.explain: Shipping the order triggers a freight charge credited to the new account 7850, Freight Out — Customer Shipments.

questions.q: What process converts the shipped sales order into a formal Receivables invoice?
questions.explain: AutoInvoice is the Receivables process that converts a shipped sales order (and other transaction sources) into a formal invoice.

questions.q: What older invoice is already open on Harborview's account, unrelated to SO-48217?
questions.explain: INV-HV-29890, for $6,100.00 from an earlier, unrelated shipment, is already sitting open on Harborview's account.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is anything wrong with INV-HV-30144 itself?
options: Yes, it is missing its freight line
Yes, it was invoiced to the wrong customer
No, the invoice generates and transfers to Receivables completely cleanly
Yes, it used the wrong discount percentage
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states nothing about INV-HV-30144 is wrong — the problem that emerges later involves how the resulting payment gets applied, not the invoice itself.
